retained_observations: ossl_ecx_key_fromdata's private import may receive a plain OPENSSL_malloc block from OSSL_PARAM_get_octet_string when the key's privkey slot is NULL; CRYPTO_secure_clear_free recognises a non-secure pointer and clear-frees it, so the bytes are cleansed, but their lifetime is not in secure memory. This is the authority's behaviour.
ossl_ecx_key_allocate_privkey overwrites the privkey slot without releasing a previous allocation, exactly as the authority; callers use it only on a fresh key.

ossl_ec_wNAF_mul's length sums and the precomputation product are unchecked in the authority and remain unchecked here; a valid points/scalars array bounds num far below usize::MAX on the x86_64 profile, and CRYPTO_malloc_array keeps its checked multiplication.
wNAF digit arrays are plain-freed, matching the authority; the secret-scalar cases are routed to the Montgomery ladder, so the arrays are not classified secret.
No constant-time claim is made for the ladder: it uses BN_consttime_swap and route-merged condition bits as the authority does, but no timing measurement was performed.
